name: Question 14
problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=4x(1-2x)-xy \\ {y}^{′}=-3y+2xy\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the Lotka-Volterra model with carrying capacity above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the prey and $y=y(t)$ represents the predators. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.$\,$ Evaluating the Jacobian of the system at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[0.5,\,0]^{T},$ we get

| $J({x}^{∗})=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} | {{field-2}} |  | $\,.$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-3}} | {{field-4}} |  |  |  |

$\,$ The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are 
{{field-5}}.

$\,$ Therefore, the equilibrium at ${x}^{∗}$ is 
{{field-6}}{{field-7}}.
worked_solution:
Let's denote ${f}_{1}(x,y)=4x(1-2x)-xy$ and ${f}_{2}(x,y)=-3y+2xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(4x(1-2x)-xy)=4-16x-y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4x(1-2x)-xy)=-x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-3y+2xy)=2y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-3y+2xy)=-3+2x\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is

$$
J=[\begin{aligned}4-16x-y & -x \\ 2y & -3+2x\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}0.5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
J({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}4-16(0.5)-0 & -0.5 \\ 2(0) & -3+2(0.5)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 & -0.5 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=-4\text{ and }{\lambda }_{2}=-2.$ Since the eigenvalues are real and both negative, our equilibrium is $\text{an asymptotically stable}$ $\text{sink}.$

Let's denote f1(x,y)=4x(1−2x)−xy and f2(x,y)=−3y+2xy.

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x=∂∂x(4x(1−2x)−xy)=4−16x−y,∂f1∂y=∂∂y(4x(1−2x)−xy)=−x∂f2∂x=∂∂x(−3y+2xy)=2y,∂f2∂y=∂∂y(−3y+2xy)=−3+2x

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is J=[4−16x−y−x2y−3+2x].

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium x∗=[0.50] to get

J(x∗)=[4−16(0.5)−0−0.52(0)−3+2(0.5)]=[−4−0.50−2].

The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are λ1=−4 and λ2=−2. Since the eigenvalues are real and both negative, our equilibrium is an asymptotically stable sink.
